item.title: Decode One Instruction: x86-64 (Windows)
item.description:
Decode the raw x86-64 instruction bytes: 48 8D 04 D9
(48 = REX.W prefix; 8D = lea opcode; ModRM byte follows, then a SIB byte since rm=100.)
What instruction is this, and what does it compute?
Answer: lea rax, [rcx + rbx*8]
1. 48 = REX.W (64-bit operands). 8D = lea opcode, reg field selects the destination register. 2. ModRM 04 = 00_000_100 -- mod=00 (no displacement), reg=000 (rax, destination), rm=100 (SIB byte follows). 3. SIB D9 = 11_011_001 -- scale=11 (x8), index=011 (rbx), base=001 (rcx), giving rax = rcx + rbx*8 -- pure address arithmetic, no memory read.
